title: Chana Masala (Chickpeas in Spiced Tomato Gravy)
summary: Canned chickpeas simmered in a deeply browned onion, ginger and tomato masala with garam masala added in two stages.
equipment: food processor or pestle and mortar
large heavy saucepan or flameproof casserole with lid

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
green chilli, chopped (leave out for mild)
Kashmiri chilli powder (plain mild chilli, not a blend)
fine sea salt or table salt
coriander leaves, chopped, plus a sprig

steps.title: Make the paste
steps.text: Pound or blitz the garlic, ginger and chilli to a fine paste. A smooth paste melts into the gravy instead of leaving chunky bits.

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Heat the ghee in the pan over medium-high heat, add the cumin seeds and let them crackle for about 15 seconds, then stir in the onion. Cook for 10-12 min, adding 1 tbsp water whenever it starts to stick, until deep golden brown. The water lifts the browned bits so the onion colours deeply without burning.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Stir in the paste for 1 min, then add the coriander, turmeric, chilli powder and 1 tsp of the garam masala and cook for 30 seconds. Frying ground spices briefly in fat releases their aroma, but any longer risks bitterness.

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.text: Add the tomatoes and crush them with the masher, then add the chickpeas, 250 ml water and salt. Bring to the boil, set the lid ajar and simmer gently for 25-30 min until thick, stirring now and then. Press a few chickpeas against the side of the pan; their starch helps thicken the gravy.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in the remaining garam masala, the lemon juice and most of the coriander, then taste for salt. Serve topped with a coriander sprig.

tips: Rushing the onions is the biggest mistake; pale onions give a thin, sharp gravy, so wait for deep golden brown.
Leave out the green chilli for a mild version; Kashmiri chilli gives colour without much heat.
Adding a little garam masala at the end keeps its fragrance bright.
Serve with rice, flatbreads or a spoon of yoghurt.
storage: Refrigerate covered up to 4 days, or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
